title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
A Kansas couple, Matthew and Leah Spurlock, were repeatedly stopped because their KU alumni license plate number, 7007, matched a stolen GMC pickup's temporary Kansas tag. In Colwich, Kansas, police received a Flock camera alert and pulled Leah over, but an officer recognized her minivan and learned the plate type had been entered incorrectly. About a month later, in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock alert led police to stop them at gunpoint, handcuff Matthew, and point weapons at them before the mistake was sorted out.

The problem is that Kansas has more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty plates, and it has duplicated numbers across plate types. Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not backgrounds, so they cannot tell a specialty plate from another plate with the same number. Wichita police say such alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but wrong entries can still lead to stops. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit, nonduplicated plate numbers. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops.
